# Rules generated by Qwen3.8-27B in the oracle loop

This archive holds Coccinelle rules for CVEhound. They cover Linux kernel CVEs
that had no rule in CVEhound.

The Qwen3.8-27B model wrote the rules. The oracle tested each rule. When a rule
failed, the model got the oracle's report and tried to fix the rule. The model
never saw a hand-written rule for the CVE, and it did not see the CVE ID.

These rules passed automatic tests only. No person has reviewed them, and they
are not part of CVEhound.

## Files

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `rules/` | One rule for each accepted CVE: 1,890 files. |
| `round1.parquet` | All 6,174 accepted rules, with details for each rule. |
| `round1.md` | Summary tables: by repair round, fix shape, year and subsystem. |

## Names

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `rules/CVE-2015-1350.cocci` | The rule for that CVE. It is the first rule listed for that CVE in `round1.parquet`. |
| `round1` | The first round of generation. |
| `pool0` to `pool3` | The CVEs were split into four parts, called pools. `run_id` names the pool. |

## Results

| Stage | CVEs | Rules |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Tried | 3,322 | 84,400 attempts |
| At least one rule passed the basic checks | 1,948 | 10,934 |
| At least one rule also passed the slower checks | 1,910 | 9,976 |
| Accepted | 1,890 | 6,174 |

An accepted rule must meet all of these conditions:

- It passes the basic checks and the slower checks.
- It is not degenerate. For example, it does not match only common words.
- A full scan of the kernel tree costs at most 60 seconds of CPU time.

Each CVE keeps at most four rules. The rules for one CVE can be very similar:
4,209 of the 6,174 rules mark different lines.

How many repair rounds each accepted rule needed:

| Repair rounds | Rules |
| ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 2,841 |
| 1 | 1,709 |
| 2 | 957 |
| 3 | 667 |

## Main fields in `round1.parquet`

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `cve` | The CVE the rule is for. |
| `rule_text` | The rule, with the `Files`, `Fix` and `Fixes` header lines. |
| `round` | The number of repair rounds before this rule passed. |
| `attempt_id` | `CVE:chain:round`. For example, `CVE-2015-1350:0:2` is chain 0, round 2. |
| `transform_applied` | `True` if the normalising script changed the model's text. |
| `cost_cpu_seconds` | CPU time for a full scan of the kernel tree. |
| `shape`, `year`, `subsystem` | The kind of fix, the CVE year and the kernel area. |
| `run_id` | The pool the rule came from. |

To read the file in Python, install `pandas` and `pyarrow`:

```python
import pandas as pd

rules = pd.read_parquet('round1.parquet')
print(rules.loc[0, 'rule_text'])
```

## How the rules were made

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Model | Qwen3.8-27B, full weights (BF16), not quantised |
| Machine | NVIDIA H200 NVL |
| Model input | The fix diff, the commit message and the file history (`P-H`) |
| Chains per CVE | Up to 8 |
| Repair rounds per chain | Up to 3 |
| Temperature | 0.7 |
| Top-p | 0.95 |
| Max tokens | 2048 |
| Seed | 0 |
| Thinking | Off |
| Scoring date | 29-30 September 2026 |
